turns.npc_reply: Eleanor Vance. Though I rather think you knew that before you sat down, Inspector.

My name is Eleanor Vance.

I'm sorry if I was unclear before - it's been such a shock. Hosting that dinner party last night feels like an eternity ago now... I know this must be hard for you as well, investigating a death in my home. Please ask me any questions; I'll do anything to help clear up what happened.

I hope we can work together and find answers quickly so everyone involved - especially the Whitmores - can put this behind them.

Oh, Charles was married to Emily Whitmore for decades. She's... she must be devastated by his death.

I saw her arrive at the party earlier in the evening; they came separately due to some tension between them lately. But I never imagined...

Poor Emily! The last thing any of us expected when we gathered here yesterday was that Charles would end up dead before dessert had even been served, much less how he ended up...

I spent most of the evening in the drawing room with our other guests. Dinner finished around nine-fifteen; we moved to the next room for coffee.

At about twenty-five past, Charles stepped out to take a phone call - I believe it was down by the study door. I only saw him briefly as he left, shooing me away so he could speak privately. He seemed irritated but not unkindly...

turns.player_input: how did you see him in study door if you were drawing room and next room for coffee?
turns.npc_reply:
The corridor outside the drawing room leads past both rooms - it's a short walk to reach either. As I was heading toward the kitchen, Charles stepped out of the drawing room into that hallway.

He didn't enter his office; he just paused in the doorway with one hand on the knob as if deciding whether or not to shut himself inside for privacy while making what sounded like an important call.
